content: Efavirenz, marketed under the brand name SUSTIVA®, is a non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NNRTI) specifically designed to target HIV-1. Its chemical name is (S)-6-chloro-4-(cyclopropylethynyl)-1,4-dihydro-4-(trifluoromethyl)-2H-3,1-benzoxazin-2-one. This compound is practically insoluble in water, with a solubility of less than 10 micrograms per milliliter. Capsules: SUSTIVA is available in capsule form for oral administration, containing either 50 mg or 200 mg of efavirenz. The inactive ingredients in the capsules include lactose monohydrate, magnesium stearate, sodium lauryl sulfate, and sodium starch glycolate. The capsule shell is composed of gelatin, sodium lauryl sulfate, titanium dioxide, and may also contain yellow iron oxide and silicon dioxide. The capsules are printed with ink that contains carmine 40 blue, FD&C Blue No. 2, and titanium dioxide. Tablets: SUSTIVA is also available as film-coated tablets for oral administration, each containing 600 mg of efavirenz. The inactive ingredients in the tablets include croscarmellose sodium, hydroxypropyl cellulose, lactose monohydrate, magnesium stearate, microcrystalline cellulose, and sodium lauryl sulfate. The film coating of the tablets consists of Opadry Yellow and Opadry Clear. The tablets are polished with carnauba wax and printed with purple ink, specifically Opacode WB.
